```python
    """
    Attached to frozen classes as __setattr__.
    """
    if isinstance(self, BaseException) and name in (
```

Wait, I should check if `__suppress_context__` and `__notes__` are available in all Python versions that `attrs` supports.
`__notes__` was added in Python 3.11.
`__suppress_context__` was added in Python 3.11.

If `attrs` supports older Python versions, `BaseException.__setattr__(self, name, value)` will still work if the attribute is allowed to be set on `BaseException`.

Actually, if I try to set `__notes__` on a `BaseException` in Python < 3.11, it might just work (as a normal attribute) or it might fail if `BaseException` has `__slots__`.
`BaseException` does have `__slots__` in some versions.

Let's check what happens if we set an arbitrary attribute on `BaseException` in Python.
In Python 3.10:
```python

>>> e.__notes__ = "test"

  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
```
